learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge and understanding of the theoretical aspects of power devices and arrangements for the static conversion of electricity with a view to the energy transition.
Ability to analyze structures used for static electricity conversion in the civil and / or industrial sector and to assess their impact on the electricity grid and the environment.
Ability to correctly evaluate the performance of static energy conversion systems based on their topology.
Ability to carry out technical discussions both of the problems inherent to the conversion system under examination and of the possible solutions to be undertaken to improve efficiency.
Continuous learning skills, using the correct interpretation of the scientific literature of the sector.

syllabus_topics: Classification of power electronic systems and converters
Circuit theory, power and power factor in the presence of current and voltage harmonic distortion
Physics of Semiconductor (Diodes, Thyristor, BJT, MOSFET, etc.)
Power dissipated in conduction and in switching
Non instantaneous switching of the line inductors
Single-phase and three-phase bridge thyristor converters
Overview of the recommended technical standards
DC / DC converter (buck, boost and buck-boost) continuous and discontinuous conduction modes and output filters
Four quadrant DC / DC converter, pulse width modulation (PWM)
Voltage source and current source inverters
R-C type snubber for diodes and power switches
assessment_rules: The course includes an oral exam, usually consisting of two questions, aimed at verifying the actual acquisition of the expected learning outcomes. To pass the exam, the student must correctly answer all the questions; otherwise, the exam will be considered insufficient. During the oral exam, the student is always required to justify their answers, either through a mathematical calculation process or clear explanations. The number of exam sessions is defined in accordance with the Faculty regulations. Extra exam sessions for students who are behind schedule can be requested from the instructor for justified reasons.
